title: Rapid internal transfer activation and role stewardship guide
content:
Purpose:

A lightweight playbook to accelerate internal transfers (lateral and vertical) with an emphasis on role stewardship: how the hiring/receiving manager, sending manager, and transferee share responsibility during the first 90 days so transfers are high-signal, low-friction, and retention-positive. This doc is deliberately operational and checklist-first — for People Ops to run a compact activation sprint rather than a long project.

When to use this doc:
- Employee requested transfer or rotation (internal mobility)
- Role reorg that moves headcount between teams
- Urgent capacity needs where we prefer internal fill over external hire

High-level goals:
1) Reduce time-to-impact: target 14 days to baseline access + 30 days to independent contribution in most IC roles.
2) Preserve institutional knowledge: structured handover so the sending team retains runway on incomplete work.
3) Protect transferee experience: clear expectations, curated learning path, and defined steward to escalate early blockers.
4) Ensure manager alignment on growth plan and success metrics.

RACI summary (one-line):
- Transferee: primary owner of learning and integration tasks during first 30 days.
- Sending manager: handover owner for active work, access, and backlog notes for 14 days post-transfer.
- Receiving manager: role steward for day-to-day, performance expectations, and 90-day success signals.
- People Ops: orchestration, checklist gating, and access remediation escalation.

Pre-transfer checklist (to be completed before official start date):
- People Ops: confirm role brief + compensation alignment and publish transfer offer to transferee.
- Receiving manager: provide role charter (1 pager) with 3 success buckets and first-quarter priorities.
- Sending manager: create Handover Snapshot doc capturing active tickets, stakeholders, recurring meetings, and outstanding risks.
- Transferee: complete internal transfer acceptance form (career intent, development goals, preferred mentors).
- IT/Security: validate access matrix and schedule account changes (2-business-day SLA).

Day 0 to Day 7 (baseline ramp and access):
- Confirmed calendar invites for: 1:1 with receiving manager, team intro, buddy pairing, and role-specific tech orientation.
- People Ops: ensure onboarding checklist completed (hardware, VPN, KMS access where applicable).
- Buddy (assigned by receiving manager): first 2 hours deep-dive on repo layout, dev loop, and code ownership map.
- Transferee: shadow an existing task; document 3 quick wins to attempt in week 2.

Day 8 to Day 30 (contribution and feedback loops):
- Weekly three-way sync (sending manager optional until day 14) to surface lingering dependencies.
- Receiving manager: set 3 measurable milestones for day 30 (e.g., PR merged, infra runbook updated, customer bug triage).
- Learning path: curated list (repos, runbooks, docs, people to ask) limited to 6 items to avoid overload.
- Checkpoint: People Ops runs a quick pulse survey on day 14 (anonymous rating: clarity of role, access, support).

Day 31 to Day 90 (growth and stewardship):
- 30/60/90 template filled by receiving manager + transferee and stored in People Ops folder.
- Biweekly progress review with steward (someone other than direct manager) to identify blockers that require org-level help.
- Sending manager: archive handover notes and surface any long-tail risks to receiving manager; flag any product/account relationships needing formal introductions.
- Career conversation: confirm if transfer is temporary (rotation) or permanent; document potential path back or onward after 90 days.

Role Stewardship responsibilities (detailed):
- Receiving manager: define success criteria with clear acceptance signals (both qualitative and quantitative).
- Sending manager: hold ownership of legacy commitments until formally re-triaged; be available for 2 weeks as subject matter contact.
- Transferee: own a short learning log and 1 internal write-up to teach the team (solidify knowledge by teaching).
- People Ops: maintain a transfer tracker (minimal fields: transferee, from, to, start_date, expected_90d_signals, status) and escalate if gating items slip >3 business days.

Interview / calibration rubric for transfer-fit conversations (for receiving manager + People Ops):
- Motivation alignment (scale 1–5): why transferee wants this role, long-term fit.
- Skill match (1–5): core skills mapped to role charter must be at least 3/5 for lateral; 4/5 for upward moves.
- Cultural fit & collaboration (1–5): evidence from peers and sending manager.
- Risk signals (free text): ongoing high-priority ownership, legal/contract concerns, required certifications.
- Recommendation and contingency: accept | accept-with-conditions | delay | decline.

Onboarding templates and artifacts (quick links and contents):
- 1-pager role charter: mission, 3 KPIs, non-goals, top 5 stakeholders.
- Handover Snapshot: tickets, owners, recurring commitments, escalations, pending approvals.
- 30/60/90 sheet: deliverables, learning goals, people to meet by date.
- Knowledge transfer teachback: 1 slide + 10-minute demo by day 30.

Quick scripts and templates (copy-paste friendly):
- Receiving manager intro email to team: "Hi all — joining us this week: [Name]. Role summary: [one-line]. Please add key context in #team-channel and welcome them to shadow any pairing sessions this month. Buddy: [Name]."
- Three-way sync agenda (30m): 1) current state & handover risks (5m), 2) first 30-day milestones (10m), 3) operational blockers & access (5m), 4) success signals and follow-ups (10m).

Contingency playbook (if transfer stalls):
- If access or critical tooling blocked >3 business days: People Ops triage call with IT and receiving mgr.
- If transferee is struggling with core skills by day 30: consider time-boxed remediation plan (30 days) with paired work and scaled responsibilities.
- If role is no longer a fit at day 60: convene sending manager and People Ops to design a stable next step (return to previous role or matched internal alternative).

Signals of success and off-ramps:
- Day 30 success: at least one independent deliverable shipped, positive buddy feedback, no critical access debt.
- Day 60 success: independent handling of routine operational tasks, improving score on collaboration rubric.
- Day 90 success: meeting 2 of 3 KPIs in role charter OR agreed growth plan signed by receiving manager and transferee.

Notes to self / open questions (work-in-progress):
- Should we require a minimal written handover (2 pages) for all transfers regardless of seniority? Pros: better continuity. Cons: adds friction for small changes.
- Explore a lightweight internal transfer badge in Slack upon completion (recognition + quick way to find previous manager).
- Metrics to track: transfer-to-impact time, 90-day retention, sending-team incident backlog post-transfer.

Appendix: short checklist (one-line items to gate completion)
- Offer accepted and salary aligned
- Role charter published
- Handover snapshot created and shared
- Buddy assigned
- Access validated by IT/Sec
- 3x calendar blocks scheduled (intro, tech orientation, 30-day review)
- 30/60/90 template added to People Ops folder

If you are reviewing this doc: leave comments inline for missing fields or local team exceptions. This playbook is intended to be iterative and will be updated after the next retention cohort analysis (Q2).

End of playbook.
